"Rouge-like platformer. Various animals leave their home to explore the world. They must fight off homesickness (measured by a meter) by seeing sights and avoiding hardships (like wet socks from puddles, ripped bags from thorns, etc.). Revisiting the same areas increases homesickness while visiting views will decrease it. Each level will lead to a new town, where homesickness is reset. In town, equipment can be bought to help with wandering (boots, umbrellas, etc.). Each animal comes with pros and cons. It should have various biomes. Graphics to be 16-bit era. (2D Game, Phone/Tablet)

Built **Far from the Burrow**, a playable 16-bit-style platform adventure in `index.html`.

Choose Pip the hare, Milo the bear, or Fern the fox, then explore four biomes. Collect scenic views to ease homesickness and earn coins; avoid puddles and thorns, or buy gear in each town to handle them. Homesickness rises as you linger in familiar areas, and reaching 100% sends you back a bit along the trail. The game includes keyboard and mobile touch controls.

**Assumption:** “rogue-like” means a sequence of replayable, hazard-filled journeys with progression through towns and purchasable equipment. Verified the game loads and the JavaScript parses.
